# Draft:LG Guggenheim Award

The LG Guggenheim Award is an annual international art prize established in 2022 through a five-year partnership between the LG Group and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. It is the primary component of the LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative, a multifaceted collaboration designed to support artists working at the intersection of art and technology.
The award recognizes one artist each year for their contributions to technology-based art. The recipient is selected by an international jury of curators, museum directors, and art professionals, and receives an unrestricted honorarium of $100,000. The initiative also funds a dedicated curatorial position at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, the LG Electronics Associate Curator, focused on technology-based art research and exhibitions.
The inaugural award was presented in 2023 to Stephanie Dinkins. Subsequent recipients include Shu Lea Cheang (2024) and Ayoung Kim (2025).
The award facilitates artistic exploration of technology as a creative medium, aiming to advance the understanding of its role and potential within the contemporary art field.
Background
LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative
The LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative was launched on June 1, 2022, as a five-year, multifaceted partnership between the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation and LG. The collaboration was designed to research, honor, and promote artists working at the intersection of art and technology.
The initiative is structured around three primary pillars:
* LG Guggenheim Award: An annual prize, supported by LG Corporation, that recognizes an artist for significant achievements in technology-based art. The recipient is selected by an international jury and receives an unrestricted honorarium.
* LG Electronics Associate Curator: A dedicated curatorial position at the Guggenheim Museum funded by LG Electronics. The role focuses on the research and curation of digital art forms, including but not limited to artificial intelligence, augmented reality, virtual reality, and non-fungible token.
* Young Collectors Council(YCC) Party: An annual fundraising event presented by LG Electronics, which features site-specific installations by emerging artists utilizing advanced display technologies, to support contemporary art and emerging artistic talents.
LG Guggenheim Award
The LG Guggenheim Award is the central component of the LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative. Administered by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation, the award recognizes one artist annually for their contributions to technology-based art. The recipient is selected by an international jury comprising museum directors, curators, and other arts professionals. The award includes an unrestricted honorarium of $100,000.
The award's stated objective is to support artists who utilize technology to address sociocultural themes, fostering a dialogue between technological innovation and contemporary art.

2023: Stephanie Dinkins
The inaugural 2023 LG Guggenheim Award was presented to Stephanie Dinkins, a Brooklyn-based artist, educator, and pioneering artificial intelligence (AI) practitioner. Through her works utilizing technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR), she has highlighted how AI can perpetuate discrimination and bias against marginalized communities.
Practice and notable works
One of Dinkins' most notable works, [https://www.stephaniedinkins.com/conversations-with-bina48.html Conversations with BINA48], is a video piece featuring a dialogue between the artist and BINA48, an AI-powered humanoid robot modeled after Bina Rothblatt, a real-life Black woman. Through this interaction, the work explores how AI systems process and learn information, underscoring the need to consider diversity in race, gender, disability, and cultural backgrounds in AI development.
Jury
* Legacy Russell, executive director and Chief Curator, The Kitchen, New York
* Tina Rivers Ryan, Curator, Buffalo AKG Art Museum, New York
* Nat Trotman, Curator, Performance and Media, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
* Xiaoyu Weng, independent curator and writer; and Anicka Yi, artist
The jury panel, composed of internationally distinguished museum directors, curators, scholars, and other arts professionals, stated, "Stephanie Dinkins's work is deeply rooted in ethics and social equity, exploring new models of machine learning based on engagement rather than extraction. Her inclusive and collaborative approach powerfully advocates for transparency, participation, and accessibility in AI technologies, particularly for communities most vulnerable to their misuse. As artificial intelligence continues to shape public discourse and impact everyday life, we highly commend Dinkins for the urgency and optimism of her investigations and the transformative impact of her artistic practice."
Award Ceremony
The inaugural LG Guggenheim Award was officially announced at the 2023 Young Collectors Council(YCC) Party at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The event was attended by: Naomi Beckwith, deputy director and Jennifer and David Stockman Chief Curator, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, Taebong Yoon, Executive Vice President, LG Electronics North America, Seol Park, Head of Brand Management at LG Corp.
Public Program
Following the recognition, Dinkins presented three new works at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum and participated in an artist talk on January 25, 2024. During the event, she unveiled The Stories We Tell Our Machines (work in progress), WisdomBot (2023), and Not the Only One Avatar Image 2023 Brain (N’TOO) (2018–ongoing).
2024: Shu Lea Cheang
The 2024 LG Guggenheim Award was awarded to Shu Lea Cheang, a Taiwanese-American artist recognized for her work in Net art, virtual reality, and software design. Cheang's practice often addresses social and political themes, including gender and digital economies, through the use of emerging technologies.
Practice and notable works
Cheang's 1998–1999 project, Brandon, was the first work of web art commissioned by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. Her 2002 internet-based project, Garlic=Rich Air, explored alternative currency systems and decentralized networks. Her work is held in several major institutional collections, including the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the Centre Pompidou.
Cheang has also represented Taiwan at the 2018 Gwangju Biennale and the 2019 Venice Biennale with the installation . In 2022, she participated in the inaugural exhibition of the Ulsan Museum of Art, showcasing her work alongside media artists such as Hito Steyerl, Nam June Paik, and Camille Henrot.
Jury
* Eungie Joo, Curator and Head of Contemporary Art at San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
* Koyo Kouoh, executive director and Chief Curator of Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art, Cape Town
* Noam Segal, LG Electronics Associate Curator, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
* Carolyn Christov-Bakargiev, Director of Castello di Rivoli Museo d'Arte Contemporanea, Turin
* Stephanie Dinkins, artist and the inaugural recipient of the LG Guggenheim Award
The jury panel praised Cheang's ability to "render the porousness between the physical and digital domains, offering empowering amalgamations for audiences to engage with."
Award Ceremony
The 2024 LG Guggenheim Award was officially announced at the 2023 YCC Party at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. The event was attended by: Naomi Beckwith, deputy director and Jennifer and David Stockman Chief Curator, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, Chris Jung – North America Regional President, LG Electronics.
Public Program
On May 2, 2024, Cheang delivered a performance lecture at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum titled "What the Heck: Shu Lea Cheang on Hacking Tactics, Virus Becoming, and Geek Farming". The program included a conversation with Noam Segal, the LG Electronics Associate Curator.
2025: Ayoung Kim
The 2025 LG Guggenheim Award was presented to Ayoung Kim, a South Korean visual and media artist. Kim is recognized for integrating emerging technologies—including virtual reality(VR), game engines, live simulation, and LiDAR scanning—with traditional mediums such as sculpture, printmaking, and performance to investigate contemporary social issues.
Practice and notable works
Kim frequently examines AI literacy through her major works. In Delivery Dancer’s Sphere (2022), she employed AI, game engines, LiDAR scanning, and 3D modeling to explore the hidden dynamics of technological society, highlighting the intensifying competition among delivery riders shaped by algorithmic optimization. The sequel, Delivery Dancer's Arc: Inverse (2024), employs generative AI to challenge Western-centric perceptions of time.
Career and recognition
Kim is the first South Korean artist to receive the LG Guggenheim Award. Her career is marked by several international accolades, including the Golden Nica at Ars Electronica (2023), making her the first Korean artist to win the award. Other honors include the ACC Future Prize (2024) and the Royal Academy of Arts Award (2010).
Her work is included in the collections of the National Museum of Art, Osaka, Japan, the MMCA(National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art), Korea, and the Leeum Museum of Art, Korea. She has exhibited at major art institutions worldwide, including the Palais de Tokyo in Paris (2016), the Berlin International Film Festival (2020), MMCA Seoul, Seoul (2023), HEK (House of Electronic Arts Basel), Basel (2023), M+, Hong Kong (2024), MoMA, New York (2024), ACMI (Australian Centre for the Moving Image), Melbourne (2024), and the Mori Art Museum,Tokyo (2025). She has participated in major international exhibitions, including the Venice Biennale (2015), the Gwangju Biennale (2018), and solo exhibitions at Hamburger Bahnhof in Berlin (2025) and MoMA PS1 in New York (2025–2026).
Jury
* Mohamed Almusibli, Director and Chief Curator, Kunsthalle Basel
* Doryun Chong, artistic director and Chief Curator, M+, Hong Kong
* Sabine Himmelsbach, Director, HEK (House of Electronic Arts), Basel
* Alfredo Jaar, artist, architect and filmmaker
* Noam Segal, LG Electronics Associate Curator, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York
In a statement, the jury said, “The work of Ayoung Kim represents a paradigm shift in how art can engage with emerging technologies, fusing traditional cinematic and graphic tropes with new image making techniques. Her work offers transformative perspectives on how humanity interacts with and understands these new tools. The artist’s seamless blend of traditional and cutting-edge methods—melding performance, virtual environments, gaming engines and printmaking—demonstrates her ability to bridge seemingly disparate worlds into cohesive, thought-provoking pieces.”
Award Ceremony
The award ceremony took place on Thursday, May 8, 2025, at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, attended by Naomi Beckwith, deputy director and Jennifer and David Stockman Chief Curator, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum and representatives from LG.
Public Program
On July 1, 2025, Ayoung Kim  engaged with global audiences through a public program, presenting her work in collaboration with LG, the Guggenheim Museum, and Noam Segal, LG Electronics Associate Curator.
Award Design and Identity
The physical trophy presented to the award recipients was designed by Lee Suk-woo, the designer of the 2018 PyeongChang Winter Olympics medals. The design incorporates the digits "1" and "0" as a motif, representing the binary system used in computing and information science. The sculptural form of the trophy is intended to symbolize the intersection of digital technology and contemporary art.
In 2023, the award's design received an iF Design Award in the Products category.

The visual identity of the LG Guggenheim Award utilizes mathematical symbols as primary design elements. The multiplication sign (×) is used to signify collaboration between the two institutions, while the addition sign (+) represents the intersection of art and technology.
Associated Programs
Curatorial Research
In March 2023, the LG Electronics Associate Curator position was established at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum to support research in digital and technology-based art. Dr. Noam Segal has been appointed to this role, dedicating her efforts to curating exhibitions and public programs that utilize technology, supporting the discovery of emerging artists, and serving on the jury for the annual LG Guggenheim Award .
Dr. Segal has curated several programs including Stephanie Dinkins’ latest exhibition in January 2024, Shu Lea Cheang's performance lecture in May 2024, and Ayoung Kim's public program.
As part of its initiative's research support, an Academic Advisory Committee has been established to conduct research at the intersection of body, art, and science, focusing on theoretical and media abstraction concepts. This research is scheduled to culminate in a major exhibition at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum during the 2026–2027 season, featuring a broad range of technology-driven artworks.
Public Programs
2023: Late Shift x Stephanie Dinkins
On January 25, 2024, the inaugural award recipient Stephanie Dinkins presented a public program titled "Late Shift x Stephanie Dinkins." The event featured the debut of new works that utilized various OLED display technologies as an integral part of the installation. The screens were used to present AI-generated narratives, exploring the physical manifestation of digital consciousness within the museum's rotunda.
2024: What The Heck
2024 recipient, Shu Lea Cheang, delivered a performance lecture titled "What The Heck" on May 2, 2024, at the Guggenheim's Peter B. Lewis Theater. The title is a linguistic play on "hacking," reflecting Cheang's long-standing interest in hacking tactics and viral metaphors. The lecture took the form of a conversation between Shu Lea Cheang and Dr. Noam Segal, the Associate Curator of the LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative.
2025: The Soft Geometry of Being
2025 recipient, Ayoung Kim, Ayoung Kim held an artist talk titled "The Soft Geometry of Being" on July 1, 2025, at the Guggenheim's Peter B. Lewis Theater. During the presentation, Kim's acclaimed Delivery Dancer series was showcased on LG OLED evo screens.
2027: Technology-Based Art Exhibition
In 2027, a large-scale exhibition will be held to showcase the culmination of research and discoveries made through the LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative.
Emerging Artist collaborations and YCC Party
Each year, as part of the LG Guggenheim Art and Technology Initiative, the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum selects an emerging artist to create a site-specific installation for the annual Young Collectors Council (YCC) Party, presented by LG Electroincs. It allows artists to incorporate advanced display technologies—such as OLED and transparent OLED panels—into their creative practice within the museum's architectural space.
2023: Farah Al Qasimi
For the 2023 YCC Party, artist and musician Farah Al Qasimi served as the collaborating artist, developing the theme Artificial Digital Paradise. The project involved the use of large-scale digital displays to create an immersive environment that examined the relationship between physical space and digital imagery.
2024: Rachel Rossin
Rachel Rossin, a media artist from Florida, USA, curated the 2024 YCC Party with the concept of "Quickening," reflecting the accelerating pace of society driven by technological advancements.
2025: LaJuné McMillian
LaJuné McMillian, an artist and creative technologist, headlined the 2025 YCC Party by transforming the Guggenheim rotunda into a fractalized universe through the concept of "Motion Witnessing," utilizing motion capture and immersive technologies to explore collective digital embodiment.
